newsitem.title: OMAN: Ramos discusses ties between Oman and Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Ramos discusses ties between Oman and Philippines.

text.p: Philippines President Fidel Ramos said on Sunday he had held talks with Sultan Qaboos and top Omani officials in Muscat to discuss the expansion of economic and political ties and a possible bilateral trade agreement.

Ramos, whose visit was the first high-level contact between Oman and the Philippines, told reporters both countries were eager to diversify trade, which he said currently consisted almost entirely of Manila's oil imports from Oman.
"We have found that there is great potential for a larger and broader relationship between Oman and the Philippines," Ramos said before his departure from Muscat.
"This potential lies both in the Philippines' rapid economic growth, progressive enterprises and large pool of skilled manpower and in Oman's modernising and diversifying economy."
Bilateral trade between Oman and the Philippines rose to 5.1 million rials ($12.5 million) in 1996 from 4.7 million rials in 1995, figures from Oman's ministry of commerce and industry show.
According to the Philippines Embassy, about 15,000 Filipinos live and work in Oman, a small independent oil producer.

Ramos said his delegation, including officials and business executives, explored areas for possible bilateral cooperation which included water resources management, energy generation, fisheries, shipping, air transport and petrochemicals.
"Discussions have begun on a possible trade agreement," he said, adding the two countries agreed to have regular consultations between their foreign ministers.
